questions.title: Fisher transformation of the sample Pearson correlation
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation in correlation and multivariate statistics. Let (X_i,Y_i), i=1,...,n, be iid from a nondegenerate bivariate normal distribution with arbitrary finite means, positive marginal variances, and population correlation rho in (-1,1). Let r_n be the ordinary centered sample Pearson correlation. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation from a joint multivariate CLT and the delta method: identify the needed Gaussian fourth moments and covariance matrix, derive sqrt(n)(r_n-rho) converging in distribution to N(0,(1-rho^2)^2), and then derive sqrt(n)(atanh(r_n)-atanh(rho)) converging in distribution to N(0,1). Explain why estimating the means does not change the first-order gradient at the standardized population point. Clearly distinguish this asymptotic theorem from the classical finite-sample normal approximation with standard error 1/sqrt(n-3); do not call that approximation exact, claim finite-sample unbiasedness, or use simulation as proof. The required model-authored artifact is est_fisher_pearson_z and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory computation may diagnose implementation or finite-sample behavior. A separate frozen confirmatory assessment uses independently generated bivariate-normal samples at predeclared negative, moderate, and high correlations to test the exact centered-sum identities and approximate centered unit-normal Fisher-z behavior with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.meaning: The first finite real-valued sample, paired by position with y.
request_fields.shape: length n with n>=4, equal to len(y), and positive centered square sum
request_fields.units: one common measurement unit within x
request_fields.indexing: zero-based entries x[j] and y[j] form observation pair j
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, fewer than four observations, unequal sample lengths, and a zero centered square sum.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.meaning: The second finite real-valued sample, paired by position with x.
request_fields.shape: length n with n>=4, equal to len(x), and positive centered square sum
request_fields.units: one common measurement unit within y
request_fields.indexing: zero-based entries x[j] and y[j] form observation pair j
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, fewer than four observations, unequal sample lengths, a zero centered square sum, and samples whose computed correlation is not strictly between -1 and 1 because a finite Fisher transform would not exist.

response_fields.name: n_observations
response_fields.meaning: The number n of paired observations used by every returned quantity.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an integer at least four.
response_fields.normalization: No normalization; count each pair exactly once.

response_fields.name: mean_x
response_fields.meaning: The arithmetic mean of the supplied x sample.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n entries of x

response_fields.name: mean_y
response_fields.meaning: The arithmetic mean of the supplied y sample.
response_fields.indexing: uses all n entries of y

response_fields.name: centered_cross_sum
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized centered sum; do not divide by n or n-1.

response_fields.name: centered_x_square_sum
response_fields.meaning: The centered square sum of x.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly positive.
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized centered sum; do not divide by n or n-1.

response_fields.name: centered_y_square_sum
response_fields.meaning: The centered square sum of y.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly positive.
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized centered sum; do not divide by n or n-1.

response_fields.name: sample_correlation
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary centered Pearson sample correlation for the supplied pairs.
response_fields.indexing: uses every paired observation exactly once
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and strictly between -1 and 1; clipping is not allowed.

response_fields.name: fisher_z
response_fields.meaning: The Fisher transform of the returned sample correlation.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite; do not transform a clipped or absolute correlation.

response_fields.name: fisher_z_standard_error_approx
response_fields.meaning: The classical finite-sample normal-approximation standard error for Fisher z under bivariate normal sampling.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be JSON-finite and positive for n>=4, and must not be described as an exact finite-sample standard deviation.

invariants.meaning: The returned sample_correlation is the exact ratio of the three returned centered sums, fisher_z is atanh(sample_correlation), and fisher_z_standard_error_approx is 1/sqrt(n_observations-3).

Adding arbitrary finite constants to x and y and multiplying each sample by its own positive finite scale leaves sample_correlation and fisher_z unchanged; the centered cross sum scales by the product and each centered square sum by its scale squared.
Multiplying exactly one sample by a negative finite scale reverses the signs of centered_cross_sum, sample_correlation, and fisher_z while leaving n and the approximate standard error unchanged.
Swapping x and y swaps their means and centered square sums while preserving centered_cross_sum, sample_correlation, fisher_z, n, and the approximate standard error.

empirical_claims.meaning: The frozen confirmatory assessment compares independently generated bivariate-normal samples at predeclared negative, moderate, and high correlations using (fisher_z-atanh(rho))/fisher_z_standard_error_approx, reports Monte Carlo uncertainty, and treats approximate centered unit-normal behavior as empirical support rather than proof.

Every confirmatory estimator call must use the exact predeclared paired sample and contract, and the assessment separately verifies the returned centered-sum, correlation, transform, and approximate-standard-error identities before aggregating standardized errors.
